gdp_nominal.note: BEA national accounts, calendar-year 1949 GDP in current dollars.

real_growth.note: BEA, real GDP change for calendar 1949 (a mild recession year).

inflation.note: BLS CPI, annual-average change 1948 to 1949. Prices fell after the 1948 peak.

unemployment.note: BLS, average of Jan–Mar 1949 monthly rates. The rate climbed through 1949 to a peak near 7.9% in October.

budget_balance.note: OMB historical tables, fiscal 1949: receipts $39.4bn, outlays $38.8bn.

public_debt.note: OMB historical tables, federal debt held by the public at the end of fiscal 1949.

gold_reserves.note: US monetary gold stock in 1949, close to its all-time peak of roughly $24.6bn.

steel_output.note: Raw steel output for 1949, about 78 million short tons (70.7 million metric tonnes).

defence_spending.note: OMB historical tables, national defence outlays for fiscal 1949.

active_personnel.note: Interpolated for January 1949 between 1.45 million (June 1948) and 1.62 million (June 1949) on active duty.

nuclear_warheads.note: Declassified US stockpile at the end of 1948. It reached about 170 by the end of 1949.

population.note: Interpolated for January 1949 from Census mid-year estimates: 146.6 million (1948) and 149.2 million (1949).

population_growth_annual.note: Mid-1948 to mid-1949 growth from Census estimates, including immigration. A placeholder until the cohort-component model replaces it.
